text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: route53-healthcheck/failures in azc (8 failures in 5m). Alert group: regional-probes. Runbook: /runbooks/route53-healthchecks.md

maya: saw the pager, hitting the monitoring dashboard now. lots of 503->unhealthy flips for the internal egress probe to 10.12.8.4:8080

steve: oncall here — any customer-facing 5xx visible?

maya: not seeing user-facing 5xxs in logs. Traffic steering did show brief shift to usw2 for a couple of minutes tho. looks like probes marking AZC nodes unhealthy?

luis: checking probe telemetry now, getting a lot of short TCP resets from probe runners. could be timeout regression.

irene: @steve @maya I'll grab the cloud console and healthcheck history. if this is a false positive we should silence alerts and rollback probe.

netops: FYI we had a canary roll last night for the "probe-runner" image (v2.3.1) to ~10% across eu regions. tagging the deploy: sha: ab12c3f.

steve: good catch. maya, can you post the probe agent logs from one runner? paste minimal snippet.

maya: pasted logs below:

```
2026-02-18T03:12:02Z probe-runner[pid=22]: start check to 10.12.8.4:8080
2026-02-18T03:12:02Z probe-runner[pid=22]: conn established, sending http GET
2026-02-18T03:12:02Z probe-runner[pid=22]: read timeout after 200ms -> marking failure
2026-02-18T03:12:02Z probe-runner[pid=22]: check result: FAIL, reason: read_timeout
```

steve: ah — previous stable had 500ms default read timeout. v2.3.1 defaults to 200ms due to upstream perf tweak. That explains the spike on noisy AZ links.

irene: immediate plan: 1) silence alert group for route53-healthcheck in azc for 15m, 2) rollback probe-runner to v2.3.0, 3) reconcile healthcheck status and un-silence when stable. anyone object?

luis: +1. I'll open the rollback and prod restart.

netops: we should also check if the Route53 TTLs caused rapid churn when probes flipped. pulling route53 history...

incident-bot: action taken: alert group route53-healthcheck silenced by irene for 15m. Incident severity: P2 (monitoring noise, no user impact reported).

steve: irene can you run the rollback command? snippet below for reference:

```
# rollback probe-runner to v2.3.0
kubectl -n monitoring set image deploy/probe-runner probe-runner=registry.redwood.io/probe-runner:v2.3.0
kubectl -n monitoring rollout status deploy/probe-runner
```

irene: running now. tailing logs...

maya: after rollback started, one runner shows the following in logs:

```
2026-02-18T03:18:41Z probe-runner[pid=45]: read completed in 320ms -> PASS
2026-02-18T03:18:41Z probe-runner[pid=45]: check result: PASS
```

luis: rolling restarts in progress across azc probe pool. route53 health history starting to recover.

netops: note: route53 healthcheck TTL is 30s, fail threshold 3 -> 90s to mark unhealthy. we'll see final state ~2min.

incident-bot: automated detection: external traffic unchanged, backend 5xx rate normal. flags: monitoring-decoupling suspected.

steve: good. once rollout completes, un-silence and watch for new alerts. also capture which hosts saw resets.

irene: rollout finished, all probe-runner pods at v2.3.0. doing a healthcheck reconciliation run: 

```
aws route53 get-health-check-status --health-check-id abcdef12-3456
# result: 34/34 OK across checked regions
```

maya: dashboard shows azc green again. route53 entries back to healthy. I'll unsilence in 10m and monitor for recurrence.

incident-bot: alert group route53-healthcheck unsilenced by maya (scheduled check).

luis: leaving extra logs and the suspected root cause note in the incident channel: probe image default timeout reduced in v2.3.1 -> caused false fail on lossy links in AZC. PR to fix default config: https://git.internal/redwood/probe-runner/pull/987

steve: nice work. action items: 
- netops/luis: patch probe-runner to explicitly keep 500ms default and add a canary gating step (owner: luis)
- infra/maya: add an alert that correlates Route53 health flips with probe image version before paging (owner: maya)
- ops/irene: update runbook with this regression pattern and rollback steps (owner: irene)

irene: handing back to primary oncall, @steve you're clear. I'll add notes to the incident ticket.

steve: thanks team — closing thread once postmortem summary is posted. :white_check_mark:
